content: Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of conivaptan by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely during coadministration. Metronidazole decreases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of conjugated estrogens (vaginal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Crofeler increases the plasma concentration of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Crofeler has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Dabrafenib decreases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Tetracycline increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. When coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, the dose of daridorexant should not exceed 25 mg per night. Tetracycline increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of deflazacort by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Didanosine decreases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Oral tetracycline should not be administered simultaneously with didanosine (chewable tablets or powder for oral solution). Use alternatives if available. Tetracycline antibiotics should be taken 1 hour before or 4 hours after didanosine administration. Efavirenz decreases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Elagolix decreases the plasma concentration of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the plasma concentration of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Coadministration of encorafenib with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Reduce the gepirone dose by 50% when used concomitantly with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Metronidazole and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. If coadministered, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half of the recommended dose if coadministered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. When coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily (for B-cell malignancies) or 420 mg daily (for graft-versus-host disease). After discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose of ibrutinib. Tetracycline decreases the therapeutic effects of ifosfamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Metronidazole decreases the therapeutic effects of ifosfamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. The use of a CYP3A4 inhibitor may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Metronidazole increases the plasma concentration of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
